as_written_in_papers.quote: In one child, a heterozygous missense variant in the TNFAIP3 gene (c.1733C>T; p.Ser578Phe) was identified.

cases.statement: Two carriers: a girl with pediatric Evans syndrome (Table 1 patient 3, the only patient listed with a TNFAIP3 finding) and her clinically asymptomatic mother.

people.label: Table 1 #3
people.key_phenotypes: Evans syndrome with ITP as first cytopenia at age 3; sacroiliitis; no autoimmune neutropenia; no second-line therapy

quotes.quote: Trio segregation analysis confirmed maternal inheritance of the heterozygous TNFAIP3 variant, which was absent in the father; the mother was clinically asymptomatic, with no history of autoimmune or autoinflammatory disease.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Evans syndrome with sacroiliitis; the authors place TNFAIP3 among genes reported in pediatric Evans syndrome. Exome sequencing was done; no other relevant variants are reported for this child, but the paper does not list other genes excluded for her specifically.

quotes.quote: In particular, A20 haploinsufficiency due to TNFAIP3 mutations has been associated with early-onset autoimmunity, autoinflammatory features, immune dysregulation, and variable Behçet-like features [7,18].
WES was performed in three patients (50%).

segregation.statement: Trio analysis: inherited from the clinically unaffected mother; absent in the father. No affected relatives carrying the variant are reported.

quotes.quote: Trio segregation analysis confirmed maternal inheritance of the heterozygous TNFAIP3 variant, which was absent in the father; the mother was clinically asymptomatic, with no history of autoimmune or autoinflammatory disease.

functional.statement: None: no functional validation or cytokine profiling.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense: c.1733C>T predicted p.(Ser578Phe). No mechanism statement about this variant.

authors_classification.statement: The authors classify it as a VUS and say it has not been reported as pathogenic before.

quotes.quote: however, the detected variant has not been previously reported as pathogenic and is currently classified as a VUS.
